sources.notes: The company's disclosures as major political donor, read on the Electoral Commission's disclosure site by the author and transcribed into the session (download #34; the crawler is barred by robots.txt). sites.name: Beetaloo Digital at Weddell
sites.notes: Added on the author's decision of 2026-11-18 (RG-027), from the NT Government's release of 22 July 2026: an exclusive 'not to deal' commitment over 185 hectares of land at Weddell, about 30 km from Darwin, while the company 'investigates its feasibility', for 'possibly two hyper-scale AI data centre campuses', powered by up to 2 GW of on-site gas-fired generation. STATUS pre_lodgement is a recorded reading: no planning application has been read. The 185 ha is the land committed, stored as the campus area. NO CAPACITY IS STORED: 2 GW is generation, not IT load. The company's claims ($40 billion, 5,000 construction jobs, 350 operational jobs) are quoted in the release, not stored. Not mapped.

set.notes: ADVANCED 2026-10-30 (research batch 5). SURVEY: the attachment index of 6,866 documents across the NSW data centre records holds three donation disclosures. ROBERTS ROAD (SSD-10330): image-only, read by OCR and by eye - the company's director and chief executive, as applicant, declared $7,500 to the Liberal Party of Australia - NSW Division on 18 June 2018 (signed 2 December 2019, filed with the EIS). The Department's assessment report says the delegation applied where 'a political disclosure statement has not been made' and that no reportable political donations were made by the Applicant in the last two years; a delegate decided it. Why the disclosure did not change who decided is not on the record. TALAVERA ROAD (SSD-24299707): Macquarie Telecom gave $2,000 and $1,500 to the Liberal Party NSW Division and $1,980 to a City of Ryde West Ward campaign group in 2020-21; with Ryde's objection, that made the Commission the consent authority. MAMRE ROAD (SSD-92743706): restricted. Next: the NSW Electoral Commission's disclosure register (not yet tried) and GIPA-003. No improper conduct is alleged or implied. UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 8, second pass): The NSW Electoral Commission's disclosure site disallows every crawler in its robots.txt (recorded). BLOCKED on download #34 (and GIPA-003, not lodged). UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 8, the author's downloads): NSW: the Electoral Commission's stakeholder register (the author's export, download #34 in part) lists 276 major political donor entities and gives no amounts; one is a data centre company, 'AMAZON WEB SERVICES AUSTRALIA PTY LTD'. CDC, AirTrunk, NEXTDC, Equinix, Goodman and Stockland are not on it. COMMONWEALTH, with amounts, from the AEC's free bulk returns (fetched by the crawler), 2020-21 to 2024-25, by side of the return (the two sides are not added): Amazon's own returns disclose $523,945 of donations made to Labor and Liberal branches; Macquarie Technology Group's own returns $316,324 to parties; the Labor Party's returns record $27,900 from 'CDC Data centres' as 'Other Receipt', not as donations (2022-23 to 2024-25). Most of what the other companies paid went to the Business Council of Australia, a lobby group, as 'Other Receipt' or 'Subscription' (AirTrunk $104,500 in 2024-25), not to a party. STILL OPEN: the NSW amounts, which sit on each major political donor's own disclosure on the Electoral Commission's site (download #34, rest: Amazon Web Services Australia's disclosures). No improper conduct is alleged or implied. UPDATED 2026-11-18 (research batch 8, the author's downloads): NSW AMOUNTS, from Amazon Web Services Australia's own major political donor disclosures, read by the author on the Electoral Commission's site (download #34, rest): political donations made of $15,200 in 2023/24, $13,250 in 2024/25 (disclosure 130644, received 1 August 2025, all 'General (not made at a fundraising function or venture)') and $10,900 in 2025/26: $39,350 over the three periods. The disclosures as read give totals, not recipients. These are NSW figures and are not added to the Commonwealth ones. No improper conduct is alleged or implied.
